newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Commissioning process underway at Galmoy - ARCON.
newsitem.headline: Commissioning process underway at Galmoy - ARCON.

text.p: ARCON International Resources Plc said on Thursday that the commissioning process was well under way at its zinc-lead mine at Galmoy in the Irish midlands.

The company, which announced a pre-tax profit of 214,000 Irish pounds in the year to August 31, 1996, said the first concentrate production is expected to be ready for shipment within the next four weeks.
ARCON also said the strengthening zinc price and dollar means that it will be selling its product into a rising market.
"Looking forward, ARCON is well positioned to capitalise on rising zinc prices in 1997," it said in a results statement.

ARCON said substantial resource increases around the Galmoy mine and identification of new mineral discoveries on the Galmoy belt demonstrated that there is significant additional mineralisation both around the mine and further afield on the company's licence area.
ARCON said its exploration activities continue in these areas and said it would also develop its portfolio of hydrocarbon assets.

The company said it is carrying out a feasibility study on development of the Helvick Oilfield in the Celtic Sea which has 5.88 million bbls of recoverable oil and a commercial declaration decision should be made by year end.
ARCON said its producing interests, Claymore and Singleton, continue to generate good cashflow while the company's licenses in Papua New Guinea abut licenses where major discoveries have been made
